input: Research breathwork retreats within driving distance

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Without knowing the user's starting location, 'driving distance' is undefined and no relevant retreats can be identified.
The maximum driving distance or time the user considers acceptable will directly filter which retreats qualify.
Breathwork spans many modalities (Holotropic, Wim Hof, Rebirthing, Pranayama, etc.) — knowing which styles are in or out shapes the search entirely.
The target dates or timeframe determine which retreats are available and whether scheduling is urgent.
A budget ceiling for the retreat will eliminate options that are otherwise geographically suitable.
Whether this is for the user alone, a couple, or a group affects which retreats are appropriate in size, format, and pricing.
Knowing what outcome the user wants from the retreat (stress relief, trauma work, certification, curiosity) determines which quality signals matter most in the research.

gold.taskTitle: Research breathwork retreats within driving distance
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate breathwork retreats that are reachable by car from the user's location.

questions.title: What city or region are you driving from?
questions.description: Identify the user's starting location so that 'driving distance' can be defined and mapped.

questions.title: What is the furthest you are willing to drive?
questions.description: Establish a maximum drive time or mileage to filter retreats geographically.

questions.title: Which breathwork style or tradition interests you most?
questions.description: Determine whether the user has a preference for a specific modality such as Holotropic, Wim Hof, Pranayama, or Rebirthing, or is open to any.

questions.title: What dates or timeframe are you hoping to attend?
questions.description: Pin down a target window so availability can be checked and urgency of research is understood.

questions.title: What is your approximate budget for the retreat?
questions.description: Set a spending ceiling to rule out retreats that are geographically suitable but financially out of range.

questions.title: Are you researching this for yourself or others too?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user is attending solo, with a partner, or as part of a group, which affects retreat format and pricing tiers.

questions.title: What do you most want to get out of the retreat?
questions.description: Understand the user's primary goal — such as stress relief, emotional healing, curiosity, or facilitator training — to prioritise the right quality signals during research.
